hunks.baseline: Once, while Jinho hyung and I were watching TV, we had a conversation like this.
hunks.sol: Once, while Jinho hyung and I were watching TV, we’d had this conversation.

hunks.baseline: “Wouldn’t it be weird if I didn’t? Turn on the TV and his face is right there. I’ve seen him so much he feels like family now.”
hunks.sol: “Wouldn’t it be weird if I didn’t? Turn on the TV and his face is right there. I’ve seen him so often he feels like family.”

hunks.baseline: On the screen, a handsome man with a lanky build was smiling brightly. Dozens of cameras and a huge crowd reacted to his every move. Flashes and screams kept going off without a pause.
hunks.sol: On the screen, a handsome man with a tall, slender build smiled brightly. Dozens of cameras and a massive crowd reacted to his every move. Flashes and screams erupted without pause.

hunks.baseline: “He’s got it all. An A-rank Hunter is basically a walking mid-size company, isn’t he? Model proportions and a celebrity face on top of that? That’s just cheating. How old did you say he was?”
hunks.sol: “He’s got it all. An A-rank Hunter is basically a walking mid-sized company, isn’t he? Model proportions and a celebrity’s face on top of that? That’s just cheating. How old was he again?”

hunks.baseline: No matter the job, there were people who made good money and people who didn’t. And no profession had a wider gap than Hunters.
hunks.sol: No matter the job, there were people who made good money and people who didn’t. And no profession had a wider gap between the two than Hunters.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t worry, man. If you wait a little longer, your day will come.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t worry, man. Wait a little longer and your day will come.”

hunks.baseline: “Try waiting another hundred years. It’ll be possible in your next life.”
hunks.sol: “Try waiting another hundred years. Maybe it’ll happen in your next life.”

hunks.baseline: I wanted to show Jinho hyung—the one who’d snickered while he teased me back then—what I looked like now.
hunks.sol: I wanted to show Jinho hyung—the one who’d snickered as he teased me back then—what I looked like now.

hunks.baseline: *I wonder what kind of face he’d make if he saw this.*
hunks.sol: *What kind of expression would he make if he saw this?*

hunks.baseline: With every step I took, dozens of people swarmed after me. NPCs from the Jin Family of Taiyuan, men and women of all ages, were looking at me with shining eyes.
hunks.sol: With every step I took, dozens of people surged along with me. NPCs from the Jin Family of Taiyuan, men and women of all ages, watched me with shining eyes.

hunks.baseline: People’s attention. Those admiring looks were burdensome, and yet a little enjoyable.
hunks.sol: All this attention, all those admiring looks—they were burdensome, yet also a little enjoyable.

hunks.baseline: It was the moment I finally understood that common game-promo line: *Awaiting a new hero!*
hunks.sol: For the first time, I understood that common game-promo line: *Awaiting a new hero!*

hunks.baseline: I waved with a smile, and a roar went up. Trailing a crowd that only kept growing, I arrived at the main hall they used for meetings.
hunks.sol: I smiled and waved, and a roar went up. Trailing a crowd that only kept growing, I arrived at the main hall used for meetings.

hunks.baseline: “They’re waiting for you.”
hunks.sol: “He is waiting for you.”

hunks.baseline: The martial artist’s face looked familiar. He was the same man who had looked at me with contempt when Lee Seogeun came to see me last time.
hunks.sol: The martial artist’s face looked familiar. He was the same man who had regarded me with contempt when Lee Seogeun came to see me last time.

hunks.baseline: Just as I was different from the person I had been then, so was he. He made an extremely respectful fist-and-palm salute and threw the door open.
hunks.sol: Just as I was no longer the person I’d been then, neither was he. He gave me an extremely respectful fist-and-palm salute and threw open the door.

hunks.baseline: The main hall looked exactly as I remembered it. The large table in the center and the scattered chairs on either side showed that a meeting had just ended.
hunks.sol: The main hall looked exactly as I remembered it. The large table in the center and the chairs scattered along either side showed that a meeting had just ended.

hunks.baseline: “You’ve come?”
hunks.sol: “You’re here.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung, seated at the head of the table, gave me a tired smile. He was the only person in the spacious hall.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung, seated at the head of the table, gave me a tired smile. He was alone in the spacious hall.

hunks.baseline: “The Lower District Sect has contacted us. It seems the Mount Heng Sword Sect is rounding up troops however they can.”
hunks.sol: “The Lower District Sect has contacted us. The Mount Heng Sword Sect is gathering every force they can.”

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know war, but I knew combat. And war was what you got when battles piled up. Having already lost so many martial artists and so much morale in one crushing defeat, the enemy would throw everything they had into the next battle.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know war, but I knew combat. And war was made up of battles. One crushing defeat had already cost the enemy many martial artists and dealt a severe blow to their morale. They would throw everything they had into the next battle.

hunks.baseline: “We’ll march north with every force we have. The plan is to strike the enemy’s main force before it joins the reinforcements.”
hunks.sol: “We’ll march north with all our forces. The plan is to strike the enemy’s main force before it can join the reinforcements.”

hunks.baseline: “When is that?”
hunks.sol: “When?”

hunks.baseline: *Goddammit. That’s filthy fast.*
hunks.sol: *Goddammit. That’s fucking fast.*

hunks.baseline: If I became First Rate within two days, I could log out. But what if I didn’t? I’d have to fight my head off all over again.
hunks.sol: If I became First Rate within two days, I could log out. But if I didn’t, I’d have to fight my head off all over again.

hunks.baseline: “This is a fight our family is staking everything on. Your presence alone will raise morale a great deal.”
hunks.sol: “This is a fight our family is staking everything on. Your presence alone will raise morale considerably.”

hunks.baseline: “Fortunately, the Five Gates of Shanxi have agreed to help us. Move with some of them in the rear guard.”
hunks.sol: “Fortunately, the Five Gates of Shanxi have agreed to help us. I want you to move with some of them in the rear guard.”

hunks.baseline: “An alliance of five small and mid-sized sects. We’ve always been on good terms with them.”
hunks.sol: “An alliance of five small and mid-sized sects. They’ve always been on good terms with our family.”

hunks.baseline: I answered without giving it any more thought.
hunks.sol: I answered without another thought.

hunks.baseline: A message appeared saying the Quest had succeeded and my Fame had increased.
hunks.sol: A message appeared announcing that the Quest had succeeded and my Fame had increased.

hunks.baseline: *Fame drops if I refuse?*
hunks.sol: *I lose Fame if I refuse?*

hunks.baseline: The Quest Window had made me an offer I couldn’t refuse. It was ridiculous, but a strange relief spread through me all the same.
hunks.sol: The Quest Window had made me an offer I couldn’t refuse. It was ridiculous, but a strange sense of relief spread through me all the same.

hunks.baseline: While I was berating myself for being a game addict, Jin Wikyung smiled broadly.
hunks.sol: As I berated myself for becoming a game addict, Jin Wikyung smiled broadly.

hunks.baseline: He was smiling, but an invisible shadow hung over his face.
hunks.sol: He was smiling, but a shadow lay behind it.

hunks.baseline: Two powers that split a region between them were about to collide. The Jin Family of Taiyuan was short on martial artists, so even if we threw everything we had into it, we’d still be at a disadvantage.
hunks.sol: Two powers that split an entire region between them were about to collide. The Jin Family of Taiyuan was short on martial artists, so even if we threw everything we had into the fight, we’d still be at a disadvantage.

hunks.baseline: I forced the thought aside.
hunks.sol: I forced the sudden thought aside.

hunks.baseline: “Um, there’s something I’m curious about.”
hunks.sol: “Um, there’s something I wanted to ask.”

hunks.baseline: “Ask.”
hunks.sol: “Go ahead.”

hunks.baseline: His tone made it clear that he couldn’t understand it at all. I had literally wiped the floor with Lee Seogeun and even brought down Jopil. Jin Wikyung had taken me for First Rate for a long time, and so had Jopil.
hunks.sol: His tone made it clear that he couldn’t understand what I meant. I had literally wiped the floor with Lee Seogeun and even brought down Jopil. Jin Wikyung had considered me First Rate for a long time, and so had Jopil.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. My realm just won’t rise, so I wanted to ask your advice.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. My realm just won’t rise, so I wanted your advice.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m telling you, you’re First Rate. Not just that—you’re a Super First Rate martial artist who’s run into the wall of Peak.”
hunks.sol: “I’m telling you, you’re First Rate. Not just that—you’re a Super First Rate martial artist standing before the wall of Peak.”

hunks.baseline: “It’s just… I’m just Second Rate, so it’s a little hard to explain.”
hunks.sol: “It’s just… I’m Second Rate. It’s a little hard to explain.”

hunks.baseline: I looked at Jin Wikyung, eyes full of anticipation, but he didn’t open his mouth. Instead, he dipped a finger into the tea that had gone cold and brought it to the table.
hunks.sol: I gazed at Jin Wikyung, eyes full of anticipation, but he said nothing. Instead, he dipped a finger into the cold tea and brought it to the table.

hunks.baseline: *信? The character for ‘believe’?*
hunks.sol: *信? The character for “belief”?*

hunks.baseline: After checking my face, Jin Wikyung let out a short laugh.
hunks.sol: After seeing my expression, Jin Wikyung let out a short laugh.

hunks.baseline: It sounded like pie in the sky. But from the moment I heard those words, my heart was pounding.
hunks.sol: It sounded like airy nonsense. Yet from the moment I heard those words, my heart began to pound.

hunks.baseline: Strangely, that one sentence kept circling through my mind, spinning round and round until I was dizzy.
hunks.sol: Strangely, that one sentence kept circling through my mind, spinning round and round until I felt dizzy.

hunks.baseline: *What had I been believing in all this time?*
hunks.sol: *What had I believed in all this time?*

hunks.baseline: The thing that had helped me most in this game, and had always told me nothing but absolute fact.
hunks.sol: The thing that had helped me more than anything else in this game and had always told me nothing but absolute facts.

hunks.baseline: I had thought of myself as Second Rate because the System had told me I was Second Rate.
hunks.sol: I had considered myself Second Rate because the System had told me I was Second Rate.

hunks.baseline: I had already overwhelmed Lee Seogeun, a First Rate master. I had taken down more than twenty wandering martial artists by myself, and I had even brought down Jopil, a Peak master.
hunks.sol: I had already overwhelmed Lee Seogeun, a First Rate master. I had taken down more than twenty wandering martial artists by myself, and I had even defeated Jopil, a Peak master.

hunks.baseline: Everyone praised me as a First Rate master and a hero, but I was still Second Rate.
hunks.sol: Everyone praised me as a First Rate master and a hero, but I had remained Second Rate.

hunks.baseline: This time, Jin Wikyung was right. I slumped against the back of my chair, looking completely out of it.
hunks.sol: This time, Jin Wikyung was right. I slumped against the back of my chair, looking completely stunned.

hunks.baseline: If I couldn’t even believe in myself, I was Second Rate. No. I *had been* Second Rate.
hunks.sol: If I couldn’t even believe in myself, I was Second Rate.
No. I *had been* Second Rate.

hunks.baseline: Wipeng showed up late and asked, looking bewildered.
hunks.sol: Wipeng arrived late and stared at us in bewilderment.

hunks.baseline: It felt like a blocked nose had blown clear. Reaching First Rate had brought a tremendous leap in every way—senses, martial arts, everything.
hunks.sol: It was like a badly blocked nose suddenly clearing. Reaching First Rate had brought a tremendous leap in every way—my senses, my martial arts, everything.

hunks.baseline: Sure enough, people’s eyes gathered. I changed direction toward a place with even more people.
hunks.sol: Sure enough, heads turned toward me. I changed direction and headed somewhere with even more people.

hunks.baseline: But everything happens for a reason.
hunks.sol: But everything happened for a reason.

hunks.baseline: As I walked, the crowd gathered like clouds. Plenty of NPCs in unfamiliar clothing were mixed in among them.
hunks.sol: As I walked, the crowd gathered like clouds. Plenty of NPCs dressed in unfamiliar clothing were mixed in among them.

hunks.baseline: My eyes met one of them. The young man looked a little over twenty. He flinched in surprise, then quickly approached and made a fist-and-palm salute.
hunks.sol: My eyes met one of theirs. The young man looked a little over twenty. He flinched in surprise, then quickly approached and made a fist-and-palm salute.

hunks.baseline: The fist-and-palm salute now came out on reflex and looked fairly convincing. But where was the Three Paths Sect?
hunks.sol: My own fist-and-palm salute now came out on reflex and looked fairly convincing. But where was the Three Paths Sect?

hunks.baseline: Guo Whatsisname nodded hard.
hunks.sol: Guo Whatsisname nodded vigorously.

hunks.baseline: In a situation like this, he was reinforcements worth their weight in gold. I grabbed Guo Whatsisname’s hand, hoping he would fight hard enough for my share as well.
hunks.sol: In a situation like this, he was a reinforcement worth his weight in gold. I grabbed Guo Whatsisname’s hand, hoping he would fight hard enough for my share as well.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t mention it. It is merely an honor to be included in the Young Master’s tales of martial prowess.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t mention it. It is an honor merely to become part of the Young Master’s tale of martial prowess.”

hunks.baseline: A complete stranger had come all this way to fight for us, and he was even helping my Fame climb. I offered my warm thanks to the freely giving Guo Whatsisname.
hunks.sol: A complete stranger had come all this way to fight for us, and he was even helping my Fame climb. I offered the ever-giving Guo Whatsisname my warmest thanks.

hunks.baseline: *Still, I’d piled up quite a bit.*
hunks.sol: *Still, I’ve built up quite a bit.*

hunks.baseline: I opened the Status Window and saw that I was about fifty short of the target. If I grinded hard for just two more days, maybe I could log out.
hunks.sol: I opened the Status Window and saw that I was about fifty points short of the target. If I spent the next two days grinding hard, maybe I could log out.

hunks.baseline: “I’m sorry. I have somewhere to be.”
hunks.sol: “I’m sorry. I have something to take care of.”

hunks.baseline: It sounded like a lie, but it was the truth. My destination had been decided from the start.
hunks.sol: It sounded like a lie, but it was the truth. I’d had a destination in mind from the start.

hunks.baseline: I pointed out a building to him as he looked disappointed. A faded signboard hung there, and the smell of medicinal decoctions rolled out thick.
hunks.sol: I pointed out a building to him as his face fell. A faded signboard hung above it, and the thick smell of medicinal decoctions rolled out from within.

hunks.baseline: And beneath it hung a small wooden plaque.
hunks.sol: Beneath it hung a small wooden plaque.

hunks.sol: [^1]: The sect’s name is written 三道問, using 問 (“question”) rather than the usual 門 (“gate” or “sect”).
